title: Complete Nonderogatory to Cyclic Vector: The General Case (All Fields)

problemStatement.formal: theorem nonderogatory_has_cyclic_vector_any_field {K : Type*} [Field K] {n : ℕ} (M : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) K) (h : IsNonderogatory M) : ∃ v, IsCyclicVector M v
problemStatement.plain: If M is nonderogatory (minpoly = charpoly) over ANY field K (including finite fields with |K| <= n), then M has a cyclic vector v such that {v, Mv, ..., M^{n-1}v} is a basis. This is the field-independent version completing the Cayley-Hamilton minpoly research cluster.
whyMatters: Removes the [Infinite K] hypothesis from OQ-05-OQ-01 -- the theorem holds universally
Resolves the last sorry in CayleyHamiltonMinpolyOQ05OQ01OQ04.lean
Completes the nonderogatory/cyclic-vector thread in the Cayley-Hamilton gallery cluster
Requires a proof route that avoids the full PID structure theorem (not in Mathlib)
Forces exploration of companion matrix similarity or direct span arguments in Lean 4

insights: The blocking step is the PID structure theorem: K^n = K[X]/(d1) + ... + K[X]/(dr) as K[X]-modules
nonderogatory forces r=1 in the cyclic decomposition, giving K^n = K[X]/(minpoly)
cyclic_iff_ann_eq_minpoly (already proven) reduces the problem to: exists v, ann(v) = (minpoly)
companion matrix approach: if M ~ companion(charpoly), then e0 is a cyclic vector for companion, and similarity transfers it to M
SQUAREFREE CASE PROVED WITHOUT RCF: For minpoly=p*q with p,q coprime irreducibles, use Bezout/CRT projections e1=b(M)q(M), e2=a(M)p(M) to decompose V=ker(p(M))⊕ker(q(M)) without PID theorem
Key lemma irreducible_dvd_of_annihilated: If p irred and p(M),r(M) both kill v!=0, then p|r. Proof: if p!|r then Bezout gives a*p+b*r=1, apply to M*v=0+0=v, contradiction
IsCoprime.mul_dvd: p|r + q|r + IsCoprime p q implies pq|r, giving degree contradiction to prove v1+v2 is cyclic
Remaining gap precisely: only non-squarefree case (minpoly=p^e, e>=2) still needs PID; squarefree case is axiom-free
by_contra + leadingCoeff extraction cleanly isolates the zero coefficient contradiction
